stem: Which method is best for separating two miscible liquids with different boiling points?
explanationCorrect: Miscible liquids form one layer, so they are separated by boiling point using fractional distillation (e.g. ethanol and water).

explanationsWrong.B: Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid.
explanationsWrong.C: Decantation works only when a solid settles or liquids form separate layers.
explanationsWrong.D: Sublimation separates a solid that changes directly to vapour (e.g. iodine).

stem: How many moles are in 4.4 g of carbon(IV) oxide, CO₂? (C = 12, O = 16)
explanationCorrect: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12 + 2×16 = 44 g/mol. Moles = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol.

topicName: Kinetic theory of matter and gas laws
stem: A gas occupies 200 cm³ at 27 °C. At constant pressure, what volume will it occupy at 127 °C?
explanationCorrect: Charles' law with kelvin temperatures: V₂ = V₁ × T₂/T₁ = 200 × 400/300 ≈ 266.7 cm³.

explanationsWrong.B: 150 inverts the ratio — heating increases the volume.
explanationsWrong.D: Volume changes with temperature at constant pressure.

stem: How many neutrons are in an atom of chlorine-35, ³⁵₁₇Cl?
explanationCorrect: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 35 − 17 = 18.

explanationsWrong.A: 17 is the number of protons (atomic number).

stem: What type of bond holds sodium chloride together?
explanationCorrect: Sodium transfers one electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by electrostatic attraction — an ionic bond.

explanationsWrong.B: Covalent bonds share electrons, usually between non-metals.
explanationsWrong.C: Metallic bonding is between metal atoms in a sea of electrons.
explanationsWrong.D: Hydrogen bonds are weak forces between molecules, e.g. in water.

stem: An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1. In which group and period of the periodic table is it?
explanationCorrect: One electron in the outer shell means group 1; three occupied shells means period 3. The element is sodium.

explanationsWrong.A: The group is set by outer electrons (1), the period by the number of shells (3).
explanationsWrong.B: Period 2 elements have only two shells.
explanationsWrong.C: Group 8 (noble gases) has a full outer shell.

stem: Approximately what percentage of air by volume is nitrogen?
explanationCorrect: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and about 1% other gases.

explanationsWrong.B: About 1% is argon and other noble gases.

stem: Temporary hardness of water can be removed by
explanationCorrect: Temporary hardness is caused by calcium/magnesium hydrogencarbonates. Boiling decomposes them into insoluble carbonates that precipitate out.

explanationsWrong.A: The hardness ions are dissolved, so filtration alone can't remove them.
explanationsWrong.C: Chlorine kills germs; it doesn't remove hardness.

stem: Which gas is mainly responsible for acid rain?
explanationCorrect: SO₂ from burning fossil fuels dissolves in rainwater to form acids (with nitrogen oxides, also a cause).

explanationsWrong.B: Oxygen does not form acid rain.
explanationsWrong.C: Nitrogen gas (N₂) is unreactive; it's nitrogen oxides that contribute.
explanationsWrong.D: Helium is an inert noble gas.

stem: Which of these is a strong acid?
explanationCorrect: Hydrochloric acid ionises completely in water, so it is a strong acid.

explanationsWrong.A: Ethanoic acid ionises only partially — a weak acid.
explanationsWrong.C: Citric acid is a weak organic acid.

stem: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?

explanationsWrong.A: +2 is Mn in MnSO₄ or Mn²⁺.
explanationsWrong.D: −1 is the charge of the whole MnO₄⁻ ion, not manganese.

stem: In the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution using inert electrodes, which gas is given off at the anode?
explanationCorrect: In concentrated brine, Cl⁻ ions are discharged at the anode in preference to OH⁻, giving chlorine gas.

explanationsWrong.A: Hydrogen is given off at the cathode.
explanationsWrong.C: Oxygen forms at the anode only when the chloride solution is very dilute.
explanationsWrong.D: Sodium is not discharged from aqueous solution; it's too reactive.

stem: For an exothermic reaction, the enthalpy change ΔH is

options.D: always equal to the activation energy

explanationCorrect: Exothermic reactions release heat to the surroundings, so the products have less energy than the reactants: ΔH is negative.

explanationsWrong.B: Positive ΔH is endothermic — heat is absorbed.
explanationsWrong.C: Zero would mean no net energy change.
explanationsWrong.D: Activation energy is the energy barrier, not ΔH.

stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by

options.C: shifting the equilibrium to the right

explanationCorrect: A catalyst provides an alternative route with lower activation energy, so more collisions succeed.

explanationsWrong.A: A catalyst doesn't change the temperature.
explanationsWrong.B: It doesn't change the amounts of reactants.
explanationsWrong.C: It speeds up forward and backward reactions equally; the equilibrium position is unchanged.

stem: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH negative. Which change increases the yield of ammonia?
explanationCorrect: 4 moles of gas become 2. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles, so equilibrium shifts right (Le Chatelier).

explanationsWrong.A: The forward reaction is exothermic, so raising temperature shifts it left.
explanationsWrong.B: Removing a reactant shifts equilibrium to the left.
explanationsWrong.D: A catalyst speeds up reaching equilibrium but doesn't change the yield.

stem: Which gas turns lime water milky?
explanationCorrect: CO₂ reacts with lime water (calcium hydroxide) to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which looks milky.

explanationsWrong.D: Ammonia turns damp red litmus blue.

stem: Which of these metals is the most reactive?
explanationCorrect: Potassium is near the top of the reactivity series; it reacts violently with cold water.

explanationsWrong.B: Copper is low in the reactivity series.
explanationsWrong.C: Iron is moderately reactive — far less than potassium.

stem: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
explanationCorrect: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, e.g. methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆.

stem: An alkanoic acid reacts with an alkanol in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to form
explanationCorrect: This is esterification: acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water, e.g. ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate + water.

explanationsWrong.A: Dehydrating an alkanol alone gives an alkene.
explanationsWrong.B: Salt + water comes from an acid reacting with a base.
explanationsWrong.D: Aldehydes come from mild oxidation of alkanols.

stem: Polymerisation of ethene produces
explanationCorrect: Many ethene molecules join by addition polymerisation to form poly(ethene), polythene.

explanationsWrong.C: Nylon is a condensation polymer of a diamine and a dioic acid.

stem: An alpha particle is identical to
explanationCorrect: An alpha particle has 2 protons and 2 neutrons — a helium-4 nucleus (⁴₂He).

explanationsWrong.B: A fast electron is a beta particle.
explanationsWrong.C: A proton has one positive charge and mass 1; alpha has charge +2 and mass 4.
